title: Remote Desktop activity and quiet background processes are separate observer states
summary: The Observer now exposes recent RDC tool activity and living background processes without treating every quiet shell or service as active work.
claims: Recent RDC activity is shown separately from process liveness.
A living TERM process with no recent activity is WAITING/OPEN, not RUNNING.
WAITING/OPEN processes remain visible in the Remote Desktop/background section and TERM actor detail.
Quiet background processes do not force the top-level status to BUSY.
Current RDC tool invocations cannot be shown before tool-history records them; this requires RDC-side instrumentation.
decision: Use separate recent-activity and background-liveness signals; never infer active execution from PID liveness alone.
rationale: The operator needs to know both that work recently happened and that processes remain alive, without returning to the earlier false-WAITING/false-BUSY behavior.
